## Summary

The IEEE registry lists four MA-L blocks and four MA-M blocks under four spellings of Wingtech Mobile Communications, almost all at No. 777 Yazhong Road, Nanhu District, Jiaxing, Zhejiang, with one MA-L block at a Shenzhen address [1][2]. Wingtech Technology, founded in 2006 by Zhang Xuezheng and headquartered in Jiaxing, started as an original design manufacturer and now names chip design, wafer manufacturing, optical imaging and communication product integration as its businesses; it bought Nexperia in 2019 [3]. That this registrant is the group's ODM arm is inferred from the shared name and Jiaxing address, not stated by a source, so parent is left unknown.

A MAC in these blocks is most likely an Android product that Wingtech integrated for a client brand, so the brand on the device is likely not Wingtech; analyst coverage names smartphone makers among those relying on it [5]. Analyst coverage says Luxshare's purchase of the business would bring it Android clients such as Samsung, OPPO and Lenovo, and that the ODM business was over 80 percent of Wingtech's revenue [5]. Wingtech was also on Apple's supplier list from 2022 and entered the MacBook supply chain in 2023 [4].

Wingtech was added to the US Entity List in December 2024 [3]. In March 2025 it agreed to sell its product-integration (ODM) business to Luxshare Precision, including Kunming Wenxun, Huangshi Wentai, Kunming Wenyuan, Shenzhen Wentai and Hong Kong Wentai, its Indonesian operations and assets in Wuxi and India [4][6]. In October 2025 the Dutch government took control of Nexperia, which Wingtech challenged in the Netherlands' Supreme Court [3]. The sold units were to pass to Luxshare, which may matter for devices built after the sale [4][6].

Radios, silicon, FCC grantee codes and randomization are not listed: the FCC ID databases refused requests from the session that wrote this entry, no teardown naming a Wingtech-built handset was read, and nothing is filled in from memory.
